climate.overview_html: Six days before COP31 opens in Antalya on November 9, the political staging intensified. Canada is presenting itself as a climate leader despite domestic policy rollbacks, with PM Carney skipping the leaders segment and sending Environment Minister Dabrusin instead. The COP31 Presidency announced voluntary targets on global electrification, waste emissions and resilient cities. EU Climate Commissioner Hoekstra declared finance talks “dead in the water,” and the UNFCCC NDC Synthesis Report confirms full NDC implementation still leads to 2.3–2.5°C by century’s end. The Copernicus C3S October 2026 bulletin is expected imminently; preliminary ERA5 projections hold October 2026 as the warmest October on record at ~1.76°C above preindustrial.

items.headline: Canada Positions Itself as COP31 Climate Leader Despite Policy Rollbacks; PM Carney Skips Leaders Segment; Methane Mitigation Focus
items.summary: Canada's delegation at COP31 is promoting the country as a climate leader even as PM Mark Carney skips the November 11–12 world leaders segment; Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin will attend the first week in his place. Canada plans to highlight methane mitigation as its flagship contribution, while domestic critics point to rollbacks on clean fuel regulations and carbon pricing. The gap between diplomatic positioning and domestic policy mirrors a pattern seen repeatedly at COP summits.

items.headline: COP31 Presidency Announces Voluntary Targets on Global Electrification, Cutting Waste Emissions and Resilient Cities Ahead of Antalya Summit
items.summary: The COP31 Presidency, held jointly by Türkiye and Australia, announced three voluntary international targets as non-binding deliverables for the Antalya summit: a global electrification target aligned with the 35×35 pledge, a target on cutting methane and other waste-sector emissions, and a resilient cities framework. These sector-specific pledge packages have become a fixture of COP architecture since the UAE Consensus at COP28.

items.headline: Nepal and Bhutan Propose Dedicated COP31 Agenda Item on 1.5°C Warming in Mountain Regions; Nepal Pushes ‘Sagarmatha to Sea’ Alliance
items.summary: Nepal's Agriculture, Forests and Environment Minister Geeta Chaudhary presented a joint Nepal–Bhutan proposal for a dedicated COP31 agenda item on '1.5°C Warming in Mountains,' citing ICIMOD research showing mountain elevations experience warming rates up to 2.2°C for every 1.5°C of global mean warming. Nepal also proposed the 'Sagarmatha to Sea' partnership linking Himalayan and Pacific island states on shared risks from glacial melt and sea-level rise.

items.headline: EU Climate Chief Hoekstra: COP31 Finance Talks ‘Dead in the Water’; Mobilised Climate Finance at $136.7 Billion vs. $300 Billion Goal
items.summary: EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told Bloomberg that talks on new climate finance commitments at COP31 are 'dead in the water,' arguing major new pledges must come from outside the EU. Developed-country mobilised climate finance reached $136.7 billion in 2025 against a $300 billion-per-year 2035 goal, per NRDC. The Pilot Resilience Fund — meant to raise $500 million by COP31 — has secured only $180 million in pledges. African negotiators have pushed for adaptation finance to be formally on the COP31 agenda, creating a potential flashpoint.

items.headline: NDC Synthesis Report: Full Implementation of All Current NDCs Still Leads to 2.3–2.5°C Warming by 2100 — ~1°C Above the Paris Limit
items.summary: A Böll Foundation analysis of the UNFCCC NDC Synthesis Report finds that even full implementation of every NDC submitted ahead of COP31 would still result in 2.3–2.5°C above preindustrial levels by 2100 — roughly 1°C above the Paris 1.5°C limit. The analysis stresses that the absence of credible climate finance commitments directly undermines developing countries' ability to submit more ambitious NDCs, and argues the $300 billion 2035 goal is structurally inadequate without reformed delivery mechanisms.

items.headline: October 2026 Projected Warmest October on Record at ~1.76°C Above Preindustrial; 13th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C; Official C3S Bulletin Pending
items.summary: October 2026 closed as the projected warmest October in the ERA5 instrumental record at approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial averages, driven by the record 2026 El Niño and rising greenhouse gas concentrations. The result marks the 13th consecutive month with global temperatures above the 1.5°C Paris threshold. The official Copernicus C3S monthly climate bulletin for October had not been published as of November 3.

items.headline: UN Deputy Secretary-General: ‘Overshoot Is Not a Reason to Surrender’ Climate Ambition; Loss and Damage Fund Operationalisation Urged Ahead of COP31
items.summary: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed called on governments not to use potential 1.5°C overshoot as a rationale for withdrawing climate commitments, stressing that the window to limit catastrophic warming remains open. She called for accelerated emissions cuts, increased adaptation investment, and full operationalisation of the Loss and Damage Fund ahead of COP31.

major_events.name: Cyclone Murasu — Made Landfall Near Nellore, Andhra Pradesh, Early November 3; Extensive Damage; Now Weakening Inland
major_events.status: Post-landfall weakening — tens of thousands displaced, extensive damage to coastal Andhra Pradesh infrastructure; IMD had forecast 100–110 km/h sustained winds with gusts to 120 km/h at landfall; system weakening rapidly; residual heavy rain expected through November 4
major_events.impact: Murasu is the second Bay of Bengal named cyclone in under six days, following Cyclone Arnab's landfall on October 28 over the same Andhra Pradesh coastline — an unusually compressed sequence driven by anomalously warm Bay SSTs linked to the record 2026 El Niño. Back-to-back landfalls have compounded damage to already-stressed coastal infrastructure and agricultural areas.

major_events.name: Florida Extreme Flooding — 1,000-Year Rain Event; Governor State of Emergency; NWS Flash Flood Emergency Brevard County
major_events.status: Active, easing — NWS issued Flash Flood Emergency for West Melbourne and Palm Bay November 2; Governor declared state of emergency; Brevard County rainfall reached 15 inches; 2–3 additional inches forecast Monday; historic king tides simultaneously overwhelmed South Florida seawalls
major_events.impact: Flooding described as a 1,000-year rainfall event in parts of Brevard County. Treasure Coast recorded 6–12 inches; Palm Beach and Broward counties under flood warnings. King tide surge sent saltwater over seawalls and flooded major roads and bridges in Miami-Dade. No tropical system was active near Florida; the flooding is driven by an anomalous atmospheric moisture plume combined with the spring tidal transition.

major_events.name: Southwest US and Southwest Mississippi Simultaneous Flooding — 10+ All-Time Gauge Records Broken Across Three States
major_events.status: Active — Arizona, Nevada and Four Corners region severely impacted; at least 10 flood gauges in three states exceeded all-time records; 19 inches of rain in six hours near the Louisiana border in southwest Mississippi also described as a 1,000-year event
major_events.impact: The Four Corners and Arizona events reflect an extreme atmospheric river. The Mississippi event is geographically separate. Simultaneous 1,000-year flooding across Florida, the Southwest and the Gulf Coast region points to an exceptional large-scale atmospheric moisture pattern; attribution research expected to examine the role of the 2026 El Niño-elevated SSTs and intensified atmospheric moisture flux.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia / Borneo / Sumatra) — 120,000+ Hotspots; Indonesia–Singapore Joint Task Force Active; Schools Closed
major_events.status: Ongoing — Joint Bilateral Task Force activated October 30; schools closed in hotspot zones; more than 333,470 acute respiratory cases across seven Indonesian provinces; air quality unhealthy to very unhealthy across Malaysia and Indonesia
major_events.impact: ~40 million people region-wide exposed to elevated PM2.5. Underground peat fires at depths up to 8 m continue even as the wet-season transition begins. Indonesia has imposed a moratorium on new clearing permits for 66 million hectares of primary forest and peatland. CO₂ release expected to drive a measurable atmospheric spike in November–December ERA5 data.

weather.overview_html: Cyclone Murasu made landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast early November 3 as a severe cyclonic storm with 100–110 km/h sustained winds, causing extensive damage and displacing tens of thousands — the second Bay of Bengal named cyclone to hit the same coastline in under six days. In the US, simultaneous 1,000-year flooding events struck Florida and the Southwest / Four Corners region on November 2, with the Florida governor declaring a state of emergency and NWS issuing a Flash Flood Emergency for Brevard County; historic king tides compounded flooding across South Florida. In the western Pacific, Typhoon In-fa continues weakening at 140 km/h, now approximately 2,175 km east of the Philippines with low probability of PAR entry.

items.headline: Cyclone Murasu Makes Landfall on Andhra Pradesh Coast Early November 3; Tens of Thousands Displaced; Extensive Damage; System Weakening Inland
items.summary: Cyclone Murasu crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur as a severe cyclonic storm with maximum sustained winds of 100–110 km/h (gusts to 120 km/h) early on November 3, causing extensive damage to coastal infrastructure and displacing tens of thousands of residents. Murasu is the second Bay of Bengal named cyclone in under six days following Cyclone Arnab's October 28 landfall over the same general coastline — an unusually compressed sequence driven by anomalously warm Bay of Bengal SSTs linked to the record 2026 El Niño. The system is weakening as it moves inland, with residual heavy rains expected through November 4.

items.source: Fox Weather / Yale Climate Connections / NWS
items.headline: 1,000-Year Flooding Hits Brevard County Florida; Governor Declares Emergency; NWS Flash Flood Emergency for West Melbourne and Palm Bay; Historic King Tides in South Florida
items.summary: NWS offices in Melbourne and Miami issued flash flood emergencies and warnings for multiple Florida counties on November 2 following extreme rainfall: up to 15 inches in Brevard County, 6–12 inches along the Treasure Coast, and 3–5 inches in Palm Beach and Broward counties. Florida's governor declared a state of emergency citing a 1,000-year flood event for parts of Brevard County. Simultaneously, historic king tides overwhelmed South Florida seawalls and flooded major roads and bridges, with water levels comparable to some past hurricanes. No tropical system was active near Florida; the event is driven by an anomalous atmospheric moisture plume combined with the spring tidal transition.

items.headline: Simultaneous 1,000-Year Flooding in Southwest US and Southwest Mississippi; 10+ All-Time Flood Gauge Records Broken in Three States; 19 Inches in Six Hours Near Louisiana Border
items.summary: The same November 2 extreme atmospheric moisture event produced record flooding across Arizona, Nevada, and the Four Corners region, breaking all-time records at more than 10 flood gauges in three states. A geographically separate event near the Louisiana border in southwest Mississippi produced 19 inches of rainfall in six hours, also described as a 1,000-year occurrence. The simultaneous extreme flooding across Florida, the Southwest and the Gulf Coast region reflects an exceptional large-scale atmospheric moisture pattern.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab Aftermath: Landfall Oct 28 Near Yanam, Andhra Pradesh; 3+ Deaths; Strongest Post-Monsoon Bay of Bengal Cyclone Since 2014
items.summary: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Yanam during the early morning of October 28 as a 'very severe cyclonic storm' with maximum sustained winds of 125–135 km/h and gusts to 150 km/h — the first named cyclone of the 2026 North Indian Ocean season and the strongest post-monsoon Bay of Bengal storm since 2014. At least three deaths and approximately 180,000 evacuations were reported across coastal Andhra Pradesh. The rapid follow-on cyclogenesis of Murasu within six days reflects the record-warm Bay SSTs of the 2026 El Niño season.

items.headline: Typhoon In-fa at 140 km/h Tracking 2,175 km East of Philippines; Low PAR Entry Probability; New LPA Inside PAR Under PAGASA Monitoring
items.summary: PAGASA's November 2 advisory placed Typhoon In-fa at 2,175 km east of extreme Northern Luzon with 140 km/h sustained winds (gusts to 170 km/h), moving west-northwestward at about 15 km/h — a further weakening from 155 km/h on November 1. PAGASA maintains a low probability of PAR entry. Separately, a new low-pressure area developing inside PAR east of Eastern Visayas is under monitoring but has not yet been named or assigned a wind signal.

items.headline: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze: Indonesia–Singapore Task Force Active; ~40 Million Exposed; 120,000+ Hotspots; Underground Peat Fires at 8 m Depth
items.summary: The 2026 Southeast Asian peatland haze crisis continues with the Indonesia–Singapore joint task force operational. More than 120,000 satellite fire hotspot detections — approximately seven times the 2025 full-season total — are driven by the record El Niño-linked drought. Underground peat fires at depths up to 8 metres continue even as the wet-season transition begins, with ~40 million people exposed to elevated PM2.5 and 333,470+ acute respiratory cases recorded across seven Indonesian provinces.

renewables.overview_html: At the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026 (November 2–5, New Delhi), PM Modi announced India’s non-fossil electricity capacity has surpassed 310 GW — more than 50% of total installed power, meeting its Paris commitment five years early, with a target of an additional 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030. Solar sector corporate funding rose 45% year-on-year through three quarters of 2026, with 88 M&A transactions in 9M 2026. South Korea launched its second 2026 offshore wind tender at ~2.2 GW. In the US, the Interior Department is seeking court reconsideration of permits for four major offshore wind projects including the partly operational Revolution Wind and the 1.7 GW Maryland project.

items.headline: PM Modi Opens Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026: India Crosses 310 GW Non-Fossil Capacity, Meets Paris Target 5 Years Early; 500 GW Additional by 2030
items.summary: PM Modi inaugurated the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on November 2, announcing India has surpassed 310 GW of non-fossil power capacity (>50% of total installed power), meeting its Paris Agreement climate commitment five years ahead of schedule. Minister Pralhad Joshi cited USD 67 billion in sector investment over the past two years. Modi set an additional 500 GW non-fossil capacity target by 2030–2031 and highlighted a proposed $200 million Africa Solar Facility. The summit (November 2–5) also hosts the 9th International Solar Alliance Assembly and 4th International Green Hydrogen Conference.

items.headline: Solar Sector Corporate Funding Up 45% Year-on-Year Through Three Quarters of 2026; 88 M&A Transactions in 9M 2026 vs. 76 in 9M 2025
items.summary: Solar sector corporate funding rose 45% year-on-year through the first three quarters of 2026, according to a PV Magazine analysis. The sector recorded 88 M&A transactions in 9M 2026, up from 76 in 9M 2025. Notable transactions in the period included Inox Solar Americas' $750 million purchase of Boviet Solar and Drax's $737 million acquisition of Bluefield Solar Income Fund. The growth reflects strong demand for clean energy capacity amid sustained data centre and industrial load growth.

items.headline: South Korea Launches Second 2026 Offshore Wind Tender: ~2.2 GW Fixed-Price Contracts; 10-Year Annual Auction Roadmap Through 2035 Published
items.summary: South Korea's Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment launched competitive bidding for approximately 2.2 GW of offshore wind fixed-price contracts on October 30, the country's second auction of 2026. The H1 2026 round awarded 1.78 GW across five projects and was oversubscribed at more than 2:1 (3.65 GW bids). The government separately published its Offshore Wind Mid-to-Long-Term Bidding Roadmap, targeting a minimum of 4 GW in annual auctions for ten years through 2035.

items.headline: First Solar Q3 2026: Cuts Full-Year Guidance, Launches $500 M Share Buyback; Record Adjusted EBITDA Margins Despite 23% Revenue Decline
items.summary: First Solar reported Q3 2026 results: net sales of $1.23 billion (down 23% year-on-year), net income of $571 million ($5.30 per diluted share, vs $4.24 in Q3 2025), and record adjusted EBITDA of $744 million (up 11% year-on-year). The board authorised a $500 million share buyback with no expiration. The company lowered its full-year guidance across volume sold, net sales and EBITDA, trimming its India module sales forecast by 700 MW. The contracted backlog stands at 44 GW ($13.5 billion, deliveries through 2030) with net cash of ~$1.5 billion. The stock has fallen 45% from its June 2026 high.

items.headline: US Interior Dept Seeks Court Reconsideration of Permits for Four Major Offshore Wind Projects Including 704 MW Revolution Wind and 1.7 GW Maryland Offshore Wind
items.summary: The US Interior and Justice Departments have sought court reconsideration of construction and operations plan approvals for at least four East Coast offshore wind projects: the 704 MW Revolution Wind (already partly generating power off Connecticut/Rhode Island), the 1.7 GW Maryland Offshore Wind project, Atlantic Shores (New Jersey), and New England Wind (Massachusetts). Interior says the filings are procedural; industry groups characterise them as part of a broader campaign against offshore wind. The Mintz firm's November 2 Washington Update notes approximately 300 wind and solar projects are also awaiting Department of Defense review.

items.headline: India’s SECI Launches Largest-Yet 4 GW/16 GWh Standalone Battery Storage Tender for Rajasthan and Gujarat; Bid Deadline November 24
items.summary: India's Solar Energy Corporation (SECI) invited bids for 4,000 MW/16,000 MWh of standalone battery energy storage systems (2,500 MW/10,000 MWh in Rajasthan; 1,500 MW/6,000 MWh in Gujarat), its largest standalone BESS tender to date. Bid deadline: November 24. The tender directly supports the government's 27,000 MW BESS capacity target by FY2030.

items.headline: Italy Adds 4.83 GW Solar PV in First Nine Months of 2026; Cumulative Reaches 48.35 GW; National Battery Storage Nears 20 GWh
items.summary: Italia Solare reported 4.83 GW of new PV capacity across 147,632 projects in January–September 2026, with Q3 contributing 1.742 GW (up 37% year-on-year). Cumulative installed solar reached 48.35 GW. National connected battery storage reached 19.98 GWh (8.34 GW power capacity) at end-September. Utility-scale solar accounted for 46% of new capacity. Italy's 8.3 GW annual renewable installation target remains in force.

items.headline: Equinor Delays 810 MW Empire Wind First Power to H1 2027 Due to US Shipbuilding Constraints; Total Capex Unchanged
items.summary: Equinor disclosed that its 810 MW Empire Wind offshore wind project off New York — approximately 80% complete — will not deliver first power until H1 2027, delayed from a 2026 target, due to US domestic shipbuilding requirements for installation support vessels. Total capex is unchanged with spend shifting from 2026 to 2027. The project has secured a $3 billion+ project financing package.

items.headline: Masdar Signs MoU with Invest New Zealand for Up to NZ$1 Billion (~US$585 M) in Solar, Wind and Battery Storage Investment
items.summary: UAE-based Masdar signed an MoU with New Zealand's Invest New Zealand to explore up to NZ$1 billion (~US$585 million) in solar PV, wind and battery storage investment, tied to the New Zealand–UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (2024). Open to co-investment with local and Māori businesses. New Zealand targets doubling of renewable electricity capacity by 2040. The MoU is non-binding.

items.headline: UK Grants Development Consent for 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire — One of UK’s Largest-Ever Solar Project Approvals
items.summary: The UK government granted a Development Consent Order for the 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire (developer: Elements Green), approved as a Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project. The site covers approximately 1,765 hectares near Newark, with about 1,025 hectares allocated to solar arrays. The project was approved despite objections from local communities and farming groups over the loss of productive agricultural land.

items.headline: Iberdrola Prices $1.6 Billion Dual-Tranche US Green Bonds at 5.40% and 5.85% for US Transmission and Renewables
items.summary: Iberdrola priced $1.6 billion in US green bonds: $800 million of 3-year notes at 5.40% (maturing November 2029) and $800 million of 7-year notes at 5.85% (maturing November 2033). Proceeds fund US electricity transmission infrastructure and renewable energy projects. Total book demand exceeded $2 billion. Deal closed November 4.

science.overview_html: ECMWF launched its experimental AIFS-COMPO system — the first extension of a major AI weather model to atmospheric composition (aerosols and reactive gases), producing global 10-day air quality forecasts in 50 seconds on a single GPU vs. ~1,000 seconds on 8,000 CPUs for the physics-based IFS-COMPO. A new Geophysical Research Letters study confirms that accelerating Arctic warming is now inhibiting net land carbon uptake in northern high latitudes, signalling measurable weakening of the boreal carbon sink. In ML weather modelling, HRRRCast becomes the first data-driven regional weather model validated to match NOAA’s operational HRRR on extreme events in near-real-time, while China’s Meteorological Administration has deployed two new operational AI systems using Fengyun satellite data for typhoon structure recognition and 4-hour severe convective weather prediction.

items.headline: ECMWF Introduces AIFS-COMPO: AI System Extends Neural Weather Forecasting to Aerosols and Reactive Gases; 10-Day Global Air Quality Forecasts in 50 Seconds per GPU
items.meta: Alexe et al. (ECMWF) · arXiv:2604.03300 · Experimental operational deployment October 2026
items.summary: ECMWF announced its experimental AIFS-COMPO system, which extends the AI Integrated Forecasting System to jointly predict meteorological variables and atmospheric composition — aerosols (AOD, PM2.5) and reactive gases (ozone, NO2). The system produces 3-hourly, 10-day global forecasts in 50 seconds on a single GPU, vs. ~1,000 seconds on 8,000 CPUs for operational IFS-COMPO. At EGU 2026, the team reported AIFS-COMPO achieves lower errors than IFS-COMPO for 5-day AOD and PM2.5 forecasts, with comparable skill for reactive gases. Charts are available on the ECMWF website. Trained on CAMS reanalysis EAC4 and operational analysis/forecast data. Remains experimental — not replacing operational CAMS.

items.headline: GRL: Accelerating Arctic Warming Now Inhibiting Net Land Carbon Uptake in Northern High Latitudes — Boreal Carbon Sink Weakening Signal
items.meta: Madani et al. · Geophysical Research Letters doi:10.1029/2026GL122135
items.summary: A GRL study finds that progressive warming is inhibiting net land carbon uptake in northern high latitudes, with moisture deficits, longer growing seasons with heightened soil respiration, and permafrost carbon release outpacing vegetation productivity gains. The findings signal measurable weakening of the Arctic and boreal carbon sink — a major carbon feedback — and reinforce the need to represent permafrost carbon processes in IPCC-class Earth system models and AI climate emulators targeting decadal projections.

items.headline: GRL: ‘Permafrost Detachment Slides’ — Climate-Driven Bottom-Up Failure Mode — Expected to Become More Frequent with Continued Warming; 150+ Documented in Mackenzie Valley
items.summary: A GRL study by Joseph Young et al. identifies 'permafrost detachment slides' as a distinct bottom-up failure mechanism documented in two large Northwest Territories events (Johnson River 2017, Redstone River 2018). Unlike typical surface-down thaw, these slides fail from the base upward, driven by decades of ~0.3°C/decade permafrost warming combined with historic wildfire disturbance allowing meltwater to penetrate to the permafrost base. The Mackenzie Valley alone has more than 150 such slides. Events of this type will become more frequent with continued warming, with implications for river systems, Arctic communities, and infrastructure in Canada, Alaska and Siberia.

items.headline: China CMA Deploys Two Operational AI Weather Systems: Typhoon Cloud-Pattern Recognition and 4-Hour Severe Convective Prediction Using Fengyun Satellite Data
items.summary: China's Meteorological Administration unveiled two new operational AI weather systems: a typhoon cloud-pattern recognition model that interprets storm structure and intensity from Fengyun satellite imagery in real time, and a model predicting severe convective weather — heavy precipitation and thunderstorm activity — up to four hours in advance. Both are deployed operationally within the CMA's national forecast suite as part of a national initiative integrating deep learning into official meteorological services.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.40641 — Agentic AI Framework Connects Extreme-Weather Probabilistic Forecasts to Agricultural and Adaptation Impact Estimates End-to-End
items.summary: Researchers submitted an agentic AI framework that couples a weather-event detection module with an agricultural impact model, enabling automated end-to-end assessment from probabilistic forecast output to expected crop, livestock or infrastructure effects. The system addresses a critical gap in operational weather services: translating high-impact warnings into sector-specific impact projections in near-real-time.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.38775 — FitzRoy: Reinforcement-Guided Diffusion Model Jointly Optimises Forecast Skill and Physical Realism for Continental US Precipitation
items.summary: FitzRoy applies reinforcement-guided diffusion to precipitation forecasting over the continental United States, jointly optimising predictive skill and physical realism via a reinforcement learning reward signal. Standard diffusion-based weather models trade off sharp but physically implausible fields against smooth, oversmoothed outputs; FitzRoy's RL guidance drives the diffusion process toward physically consistent outputs while retaining forecast skill. Results are evaluated against MRMS radar observations and standard probabilistic metrics.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.36186 — HRRRCast: First Data-Driven Regional Weather Model to Match NOAA’s Operational HRRR on Extreme Events in Near-Real-Time
items.summary: HRRRCast is presented as the first data-driven regional weather model demonstrated to match the skill of NOAA's operational HRRR on extreme weather events while running in near-real-time. The 31-page paper validates performance against verified high-impact events including severe convective outbreaks and extreme precipitation episodes, and describes an operational deployment pathway for hybrid HRRR/HRRRCast products — a credibility milestone for ML-based regional forecasting adoption.

items.headline: Google DeepMind AI Model Beat Physics-Based Forecasts on Hurricane Isaias Track — Correctly Forecast Florida Panhandle Landfall Where Physics Models Said Louisiana; Intensity Gap Persists
items.summary: NPR reports Google DeepMind's AI weather model outperformed traditional physics-based models on the track forecast for Hurricane Isaias (Category 2, Florida Panhandle landfall), correctly indicating the Florida Panhandle while physics-based models pointed to Louisiana. ECMWF's AIFS showed the second-strongest track performance in the 2026 Atlantic season. However, AI trailed the NHC's blended consensus on intensity — a persistent gap — and interpretability concerns remain: forecasters cannot explain why the model produces a given correct or incorrect forecast.

items.title: CESC/Purvah Green Extends ReNew 1.4 GWp Acquisition Deadline to November 21 — ~$510 M Deal Still Pending
items.body_html: India’s CESC Limited and its renewable arm Purvah Green Power have amended the share purchase agreement for their ~1.4 GWp ReNew Solar Power acquisition, extending the closing deadline 21 days to November 21, 2026. The deal covers six SPVs holding approximately 1.4 GWp of contracted operating solar capacity at an enterprise value of ~₹4,859 crore (~US$510 million), with more than 90% contracted with SECI.

items.title: Vaisala Completes Acquisition of AI Weather Company Atmo, Inc. — USD 70 M Fixed + Up to USD 60 M Earn-Out; Deepens AI Forecasting Strategy
items.body_html: Finnish measurement technology leader Vaisala completed the acquisition of AI weather forecasting company Atmo, Inc. on October 29, four months after announcing the deal. The fixed purchase price was USD 70 million, paid mainly in cash and Vaisala Series A shares, with a contingent earn-out of up to USD 60 million tied to 2026–2028 performance targets. Vaisala said the deal “supports Vaisala’s strategic priority to grow its services and software revenue” alongside its traditional hardware and sensor businesses.

items.title: Boralex Acquires UK Onshore Wind Developer Wind2 — ~350 MW Advanced Pipeline in Scotland, England and Wales; Lifts UK Portfolio to ~2 GW
items.body_html: Canadian renewable producer Boralex completed the acquisition of UK onshore wind developer Wind2 on October 29, adding approximately 350 MW of advanced-stage projects across Scotland, England and Wales and lifting its total UK development pipeline to approximately 2 GW alongside 73 MW under construction. Boralex was taken private by La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec in August 2026.

items.title: Equitix Completes £155 M Beatrice Offshore Wind Stake Purchase from TRIG — Now 35% Owner of 588 MW Scottish Project; TRIG Fully Exits
items.body_html: Equitix completed the purchase of TRIG’s 17.5% stake in the 588 MW Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm for approximately £155 million on October 29, lifting its holding to 35%. SSE Renewables (40%) and Red Rock Renewables (25%) retain the remainder. The transaction, first announced July 2026, completed on schedule. Beatrice has been operating since 2019 off the Caithness coast.

items.title: Neighborhood Sun Acquires Meadow Energy and Its New York Community Solar Portfolio — Doubles Portfolio to 600+ MWdc; 30,000+ Subscribers Transferred
items.body_html: Neighborhood Sun acquired Meadow Energy and its New York community solar portfolio, doubling total managed capacity from ~300 MWdc to more than 600 MWdc and quadrupling its New York state presence. The deal transfers 67 Meadow Energy projects and more than 30,000 subscribers to Neighborhood Sun’s platform. Climate First Bank facilitated the transaction. Neighborhood Sun now operates in Maryland, eight additional states and Washington D.C., with more than 200 community solar projects.

items.title: IGNIS Closes Sale of 656 MWp Italian Renewable Portfolio to flyRen Energy Group — 28 Projects; flyRen Now Manages Over 2 GW in Italy
items.body_html: Spanish developer IGNIS closed the sale of 656 MWp across 28 renewable projects in Italy to flyRen Energy Group SpA, majority-owned by Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II. The portfolio covers PV, battery-hybrid and wind projects held through 23 SPVs. With the transaction, flyRen’s managed Italian portfolio surpasses 2 GW.

items.title: Tokyo Century Acquires 50% Stake in 212 MW UK Solar and Wind Portfolio from Egg Power
items.body_html: Tokyo Century agreed to acquire a 50% stake in a 212 MW UK renewable portfolio from Egg Power, comprising a solar farm, a solar development project and a wind farm. The deal adds the Japanese trading and leasing conglomerate to a growing list of Asian corporates building UK clean energy positions ahead of the country’s 2030 clean power target.

items.title: Optivolt Raises $32 Million Series A to Scale Module-Level Solar Power Electronics — 99.4% Conversion Efficiency Claimed; Total Funding $42 M
items.body_html: Optivolt, a San Francisco startup developing module-level power electronics for solar panels, closed a $32 million Series A led by VXI Capital, with RA Capital, Valo Ventures, Atlas Innovate and former SunPower CEO Tom Werner participating. The company’s Power Balancer dynamically redistributes current among solar cell groups in real time, claiming 99.4% conversion efficiency and recovering output lost to shading and mismatch. Total funding: $42 million.
